text:
nina (Design): Quick review request: compact scrubber iteration + sampled-state affordance. Proto: https://redwood.design/mini/scrub-sampled :link:

tess (Frontend): Is this primarily for medium panels where the p95 pill collides with scrubber? Or also for mobile?

nina (Design): Medium panels first. Goal: reduce visual clutter and make sampled vs exact explicit without shouting.

omar (Observability): Customers keep assuming heatmap = full data. We should surface sample ratio and give a clear path to request exact compute (async).

infra-bot: Staging: heatmap v3 running. Note CPU on low-end GPUs increased ~6% after pattern experiment.

rachel (A11y): Accessibility quick notes: do not rely on color alone. Provide a text fallback via tooltip and an opt-in pattern overlay for high-contrast mode. Ensure chip text contrast >=4.5:1 or include an icon+label combo.

tess (Frontend): Proposed behavior: collapse p95 pill to icon+abbr under 420px. Icon has aria-label="p95 118ms; sampled (1:8)". Clicking opens a small panel with: sample ratio, selected range, "Compute exact p95" CTA. Keyboard: Scrubber focused -> press S to open panel.

nina (Design): Copy suggestions: chip (short) = "Sampled"; panel header = "Estimated from sampled traces"; panel body = "Sample ratio 1:8. Request exact computation (async)."); button = "Compute exact p95". Use amber tone, not error red.

omar (Observability): Backend constraints: full computation is queued; API returns {job_id, eta}. Recommend rate limits: 20 requests/min/org and cache results for 10 minutes to avoid repeated work. We'll push job updates over websocket so UI can show progress.

rachel (A11y): Keyboard flow: panel must trap focus, announce queue status via aria-live="polite" (e.g., "Full p95 computation queued. ETA 2 minutes"). Also include an accessible explanation link "Why compute takes time" for screen readers.

tess (Frontend): Implementation note: avoid extra canvas draws for patterns. Plan: default = color-only; patterns only when user enables high-contrast or prefers-reduced-vision. Use lightweight SVG overlay in those modes. I'll prototype both to measure perf.

nina (Design): Decisions for sprint: 1) compact icon chip under 420px labeled "Sampled"; 2) panel with ratio + async CTA + ETA; 3) patterns opt-in via settings/high-contrast only; 4) keyboard shortcut S when scrubber focused; 5) rate limit guardrails per omar.

omar (Observability): I'll add telemetry items: range length, sample ratio, compute requested, job durations, p95 delta. QA: include a no-sampling baseline case.

rachel (A11y): I'll run colorblind sims and keyboard walkthroughs once prototype is in staging.

tess (Frontend): Will upload a prototype by EOD Wed.

nina (Design): Thanks all  leaving open for copy tweaks.
